JobKind.description: The kind of long-running operation a job wraps.

oneOf.description: `rocky run` — materializes tables. Takes the mutation permit.
`rocky plan` — previews and persists a plan. Non-mutating; no permit.
`rocky apply` — executes a persisted plan. Takes the mutation permit.
`rocky review <plan_id> --approve` — writes the sign-off marker that unblocks `apply`. Takes the mutation permit, so an approval cannot land while a run or an apply is in flight.
`rocky test` — runs the models' tests in local DuckDB. Reads the project, writes no warehouse state; no permit.
`rocky ci` — compile + test without warehouse credentials. Non-mutating; no permit.

`rocky policy freeze` — the kill switch: records a freeze decision in the policy-decision ledger (and a durable marker on a remote `[state]`). Takes the mutation permit: even on a remote `[state]` backend it opens the local store, which a run holds for its whole run. A browser freeze is refused (`409 mutation_in_progress`) while a run, apply or approve is in progress; retry once it finishes, or cancel that job.
`rocky policy unfreeze` — lifts a freeze. Takes the mutation permit.

`rocky preview create` — registers a branch in the state store and copies the unchanged models into the warehouse schema `branch__<name>`. Takes the mutation permit: it opens the state store for write and writes warehouse objects. It reads production tables and writes only the branch schema; it does not re-run the changed models (`run_status` is `planned`). `preview diff` and `preview cost` are not jobs.

`rocky plan promote <branch>` — runs the branch's approval and breaking-change gates and writes a promote plan. It writes no warehouse object and no state: the plan file is the only output, and applying it (`rocky apply <plan_id>`, kind `apply`) is what replaces production tables. Non-mutating; no permit. The server refuses it unless `[branch.approval] required = true`.

`rocky product approve <name>` — approves the product's current working spec: writes an immutable digest-addressed snapshot file and records the approval, the loop state and a journal row in one state-store transaction. Takes the mutation permit. The record names the server's git identity and the channel `http_api`; it does not prove a browser made the call.

`rocky compact <table>` or `rocky compact --catalog <name>` — writes a compaction plan (`OPTIMIZE` and `VACUUM` per table) to `.rocky/plans/`. It writes no warehouse object and runs no statement, so it takes no permit. For a replication pipeline, `--catalog` asks the source adapter to discover tables. Applying the plan (`apply`, with the returned `plan_id`) is what runs the statements.
The subprocess exited non-zero, or could not be launched.
`POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` signalled the subprocess, and it then exited non-zero. A job that exits 0 after the signal is `succeeded`: it finished before the signal could stop it.

description:
Status of a `rocky serve` long-running job (`GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}`).

The presentation type over `rocky-core`'s `PersistedJob`: it carries the same lifecycle facts with typed [`JobKind`]/[`JobState`] enums for embedder ergonomics, and — once the job is terminal — the canonical `RunOutput` / `PlanOutput` / `ApplyOutput` the underlying subprocess emitted, embedded **verbatim** in [`result`](Self::result). An embedder switches on [`kind`](Self::kind) to know which schema `result` conforms to (the same `run` / `plan` / `apply` schemas the CLI exports).

error.description: Failure detail when [`state`](Self::state) is [`JobState::Failed`], what stopped the job when it is [`JobState::Cancelled`], else `null`.

finished_at.description: When the job reached a terminal state (RFC 3339), or `null` if not yet.

principal.description: The advisory, spoofable `X-Rocky-Principal` recorded for audit, or `null`. Never an authorization input under the single-shared-secret auth ceiling.

result.description: The canonical output of the underlying `rocky <kind>` command, embedded verbatim once the job is terminal (`null` while queued/running). Its shape is the `run` / `plan` / `apply` schema selected by [`kind`](Self::kind).

started_at.description: When execution started (RFC 3339), or `null` if not yet.
